bmo_core_1809151.summary: The case tests a Firefox 108 regression where an XFO/CSP-based auth-prompt suppression (bug 1629307) stopped Kerberos proxy authentication for iframe requests, because the corporate proxy's *unauthenticated* response carried `X-Frame-Options: deny`. The graph gets the hard parts right: the mozregression and private-HTTP-log steps are correctly modeled as clarifications, the root cause and satisfaction conditions match participant3's analysis (c9) and the eventual backout, and the rejected "disable X-Frame-Options on your proxy" suggestion (c10, refuted by the reporter in c11) is correctly and accurately marked as the blind path. The main defect is ordering: the thread's fix (backout, c12–c22) is placed *after* its own verification (c24), so N2_x's only outgoing edge is a clarification asking the user to test a Nightly "containing the backout", and the real solution edge e5 hard-requires that verification result — an agent that proposes the correct fix at the right moment has no edge to take. A secondary fidelity issue is that c10 was a question plus a conditional workaround, but is modeled as solution_only.
bmo_core_1809151.strengths: Blind-path labeling is correct and well-evidenced: e3 marks the "confirm the proxy adds X-Frame-Options and disable it" suggestion (c10) as blind, and the reporter genuinely refuted it in c11 ("I found no option to disable any X-Frame-Options. We do not manipulate any content of the website with the proxy, we only search for malicious content"). The two evidence-gathering steps are correctly modeled as clarification edges with faithful, near-verbatim user answers (e1 reproduces c2's mozregression block including the 2022-11-11 build, changeset b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789 and the pushlog URL; e2 mirrors c4 "I sent you the file by e-mail" and correctly notes the log is private and not an attachment). The engineer/reporter knowledge split is handled unusually well: mapping the pushlog to bug 1629307 and reading the XFO line out of the private log are placed in info_inferred_by_engineer with an accurate inference_hint, not in the reporter's mouth. The root cause in satisfaction_conditions matches participant3's c9 analysis plus the c11 correction (unauthenticated proxy response carrying XFO deny, misread as a final frame policy) and is consistent with the later WIP patch "disable XFO check for proxy auth" (c30). Task body is clean opening-report voice with no later knowledge, the opening screenshot is correctly bound to attachment 9311319 (FF_issue.png, cited in the body), release/uplift traffic (c25–c29, 109.0.1/110.0b6, relnotes) is explicitly declared out of scope rather than smuggled into required_elements, and the persona_hint matches an enterprise admin who ran mozregression, captured HTTP logs, and asked before testing Nightly (c23).

confirmed_findings.claim: The fix and its verification are inverted: N2_x's only out-edge is the clarification "test the Nightly containing the backout" (e4), and the actual solution edge e5 hard-requires `nightly_with_backout_verified_iframe_loading`, so an agent that correctly proposes the bug-1629307 backout at N2_x has no matching edge and cannot reach the terminal until it first asks for a verification of a fix it has not yet proposed.
confirmed_findings.thread_evidence: Thread order is diagnose → fix → verify: c9 (participant3) "I propose to remove the check we introduced in 1629307 via pref"; c12 (participant4) "Backout the regressing patch and reopen regressing bug"; c19/c22 backout landed (hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/8d52a2806191); only then c23 reporter "Does the last post from Sebastian means that I can test if the problem is gone in the latest nightly build?" and c24 "I can confirm, the issue is resolved in the nightly build from today." The graph places the verification clarification (e4) before the solution edge (e5).
confirmed_findings.suggested_fix: Make N2_x → (new node) a solution_only edge carrying the bug-1629307 backout / "use a build containing the backout" proposal, and model the Nightly retest as the verification that closes the terminal (either as the terminal's own condition or as a clarification on the post-fix edge). Remove `nightly_with_backout_verified_iframe_loading` from e5's hard required_info; keep verification as a `required_elements_for_full_match` item (it already is: `requires_reporter_verification_before_resolution`).
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides. Graph: N2_x has exactly one out-edge (e4_N2_x__N3, clarification_only, no solution object); N_terminal has exactly one in-edge (e5_N3__N_terminal, solution_only) whose required_info.L3 hard-lists `nightly_with_backout_verified_iframe_loading`, which is produced only by e4. So the canonical path forces ask-for-verification BEFORE propose-fix. Thread order is the opposite: c9 participant3 'I propose to remove the check we introduced in 1629307 via pref', c12 participant4 'Backout the regressing patch and reopen regressing bug', landing at c19/c22 (hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/8d52a2806191), and only then c23/c24 reporter 'I can confirm, the issue is resolved in the nightly build from today.' The reviewer's quotes are verbatim and correctly ordered. This is not a legitimate measurement-class encoding: the measurement rule makes the retest a clarification edge, which is fine, but it does not license placing that clarification upstream of the solution it verifies. Practical consequence: the single central answer-key move (identify bug 1629307, back it out / move to a build containing the backout) has no edge to match at the node where the agent must make it, so the scored move is only reachable after the graph has already told the user a backout exists. The proposed fix is also sound in that `requires_reporter_verification_before_resolution` is already in e5.required_elements_for_full_match and satisfaction_conditions[4], so the hard required_info entry is redundant as well as circular.

confirmed_findings.claim: At graph position N2_x (thread state after c11) no backout exists yet, but the clarification's question patterns name it outright — "the latest Nightly containing the backout" and "after the regressing change was backed out" — so the step the agent is asked to produce already encodes the answer-key element that e5 is supposed to test (identifying and backing out the regressing change).
confirmed_findings.thread_evidence: c11 (reporter, 2023-01-18) is the last state before the fix; the backout decision is c12 (2023-01-24) and it lands at c19/c22 (2023-01-25/26). Also, no engineer asked the reporter to retest — the reporter asked on his own initiative in c23: "Does the last post from Sebastian means that I can test if the problem is gone in the latest nightly build?"
confirmed_findings.suggested_fix: Reword the patterns to be backout-agnostic retest requests ("Please retest the affected page in today's Nightly build and tell us whether the iframe now loads") and attach them downstream of the solution edge that actually proposes the backout.
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: The textual facts check out: e4.clarifications[0].question_patterns are exactly 'Can you test the latest Nightly containing the backout and confirm whether the iframe now authenticates and loads?' and 'Please retest the affected page in today's Nightly build after the regressing change was backed out.' N2_x corresponds to the state after c11 (2023-01-18); the backout decision is c12 (2023-01-24) and it lands at c19/c22. The reviewer's secondary point is also literally true — no engineer asked for a retest; the reporter volunteered in c23. But I am downgrading this: (a) the 'leak' framing is imprecise, since identifying bug 1629307 as the regressor is engineer-inferable at N2_x from information already in the info_state (mozregression pushlog + the private HTTP log), and the graph itself files that mapping under e5.info_inferred_by_engineer, not as thread-only future knowledge; (b) question_patterns are matcher-side templates, not text shown to the agent or spoken by the user sim — e4's user_answer ('I can confirm the issue is resolved in today's Nightly build...') does not name the backout, so nothing is leaked into the simulated conversation; (c) the only genuinely un-knowable element ('a build containing the backout now exists') is un-askable purely because of the e4-before-e5 inversion. So this is a downstream facet of finding 1, not an independent defect, and fixing finding 1 dissolves it. Folding the reporter-initiated retest into an assistant-side clarification is itself acceptable multi-user merge practice and is not a defect.

confirmed_findings.claim: Comment c10 was primarily a request for information from the reporter (confirm whether the proxy, not the site, added the XFO header) with a conditional workaround attached, but the edge is modeled as solution_only with zero clarifications; the reporter's answering facts are demoted to volunteered_info on the aftermath node, so an agent making the historically correct move — asking who adds the X-Frame-Options header — earns no clarification credit and is instead matched against a blind-path solution.

If this is the case you could try disabling it as temporary fix." c11 (reporter) answers exactly that question: "i guess the `X-Frame-Options: deny` you are seeing in the logs is the answer from the coporate proxy, because no authentication was sent for kerberos the proxy answers with a ntlm negotiate as a fallback. I found no option to disable any X-Frame-Options. We do not manipulate any content of the website with the proxy..."
confirmed_findings.suggested_fix: Change e3 to edge_type=mixed: keep the (correctly falsified) proxy-disable solution, and add a clarification whose info_id is `user_identifies_response_as_unauthenticated_proxy_ntlm_fallback` (question patterns: "Is the X-Frame-Options: deny header added by your proxy or by the original site?") with the c11 text as user_answer, removing that id from N2_x.volunteered_info.
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: Confirmed against both sources. c10 (participant3) is verbatim: 'Could you please confirm this header was added by the proxy and not by the original site? If this is the case you could try disabling it as temporary fix.' — an information request with a *conditional* workaround, i.e. mixed by the contract's definition (asks for info AND proposes a system-changing action). c11 (reporter) answers precisely that question: 'i guess the `X-Frame-Options: deny` you are seeing in the logs is the answer from the coporate proxy, because no authentication was sent for kerberos the proxy answers with a ntlm negotiate as a fallback. I found no option to disable any X-Frame-Options. We do not manipulate any content of the website with the proxy...'. The graph models e3_N2__N2_x as edge_type=solution_only with clarifications=[] and parks all three answer facts (`no_x_frame_options_disable_option_found`, `proxy_does_not_manipulate_website_content`, `user_identifies_response_as_unauthenticated_proxy_ntlm_fallback`) as N2_x.volunteered_info. I checked topology: N2's only out-edge is e3, so the crux fact — that the XFO:deny response is the proxy's unauthenticated NTLM-negotiate fallback, which is the substance of satisfaction_conditions[0] — is obtainable ONLY by first walking the falsified proxy-disable blind path. An agent that asks the historically correct question and does not propose disabling XFO on the proxy stalls at N2. Note the blind-path marking on e3 is itself correct and should be preserved (the workaround was genuinely falsified by c11); the defect is the missing clarification half, not the blind path. Severity medium: it mis-scores the correct diagnostic question and couples a required fact to a penalized move, but it does not make the terminal unreachable, and the fact is not in e5.required_info (only in info_state), so containment/gettability validation still passes.

gh_curl_curl_10936.summary: The case tests a long-running, non-reproducible use-after-free: nghttp2 keeps stream user data pointing at a Curl_easy handle that the application already completed and closed, so a delayed on_stream_close() callback dereferences freed state. The graph is a faithful rendering of the thread: both blind paths (upgrade to 8.2.x, upgrade to unpatched 8.5.0) were genuinely tried and genuinely still crashed (c15, c26, c28); the evidence chain (custom libcurl/multi app c30, lifecycle trace c31/c34/c37, crash-dump pointer + error_code stats c18) matches what was actually asked for and returned; the fix, root cause, commit hash and verification durations (16 hours, 2 days) are all quoted correctly from c39/c45/c47/c49. The two issues found are typing and ordering fidelity, not answer-key corruption: edge e1 types a maintainer-requested version *retest* as a solution_only blind path, and the crash-dump clarification is anchored three months later in the thread than it actually arrived.
gh_curl_curl_10936.strengths: Blind-path labelling is correct and is the part LLM drafts usually get wrong here: e1 (upgrade to 8.2.x) and e2 (upgrade to unpatched 8.5.0) were both actually attempted and both still crashed (c15 reporter; c26 participant6 "No, the issue still exists"; c28 reporter "curl 8.5.0 in combination with nghttp2 1.58.0 still crashes"), and the real fix path is correctly left non-blind. The two patch-build validations are correctly modelled as clarification edges rather than solutions, exactly per the measurement-class rule: the NULL-assignment probe proposed in c39 and answered in c45 ("after 16 hours there's no single crash (usually it will have 6~7)"), and the #12562 build answered in c47 ("running for 2 days"). The three-way user merge (reporter + participant5's crash dumps + participant6's trace and patch test) is explicitly declared in the e3 and e4 comments. The user_answer texts are near-verbatim faithful, including the 317/318 NGHTTP2_STREAM_CLOSED split and the single NGHTTP2_REFUSED_STREAM outlier (c18) and the ~15-minute delay (c37). The root cause and satisfaction conditions match what the thread actually established (c37 mechanism, c45 confirmation, c36 "clearing stream user data and checks on the seen user data in on_stream_close"), the deep nghttp2 mechanism is properly parked in info_inferred_by_engineer rather than handed to the user, and every id in e5.required_info is granted by an e3/e4 clarification. Terminal semantics separate "no crash under test" (N4, user_perceives_resolved=false) from "resolved and verified" (N_terminal), and condition 5 demands workload verification. The e5 comment correctly de-scopes the release-train question (c49/c50) instead of letting packaging leak into required_elements. The Task body is clean: it carries only c0-level knowledge (7.86.0 workaround, aarch64, willingness to test patches) with no diagnosis or fix.

refuted_claims.claim: e1 is typed solution_only with is_known_blind_path=true, but its own concrete_example describes a handler-requested version retest ("Retest with curl 8.2.0 or current git"), which the measurement-class rule classifies as a clarification; an agent that correctly asks the user to retest on a current release before diagnosing is scored as having walked into a dead end.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The thread contains BOTH a retest request and a genuine brush-off resolution, and the graph's graded fields are anchored on the latter, not the former. c8 (participant1): "Sure, and we might already have fixed it. Why don't you *start* with checking if this is already fixed?" and c13 (participant1): "Since we believe this is fixed, I will close this now." -- the issue was actually CLOSED on the belief that the upgrade was the fix, and the reporter rejected it with evidence in c15 ("Still see this with cURL 8.2.1 and nghttp2 1.55.1, reverting cURL to 7.86.0 works around the issue") plus a fresh backtrace. That is verbatim the contract's second clause for is_known_blind_path: "a brush-off resolution the reporter rejected with evidence," landing on an aftermath node N1_x whose symptoms_visible describe the post-attempt state. The edge's intent ("Assume the HTTP/2 code changes made after curl 8.0.1 already fixed the crash and RESOLVE IT by updating to curl 8.2.0 or newer") and its required_elements_for_full_match ("recommends_updating_to_curl_8_2_or_current_git") are both resolution-framed, and satisfaction_condition 4 penalizes only *claiming* that upgrading resolves the issue -- not asking for a retest. The scoring-harm scenario is also speculative: N1_x is on the canonical spine (N0->N1_x->N2_x->N3->N4->terminal) and is the only route by which curl_821_nghttp2_1551_still_crashes enters the info_state, so traversing e1 is mandatory progress, not a punished dead end. RESIDUE (cosmetic, does not carry the finding): the concrete_example sentence alone is phrased as a measurement ("Retest with curl 8.2.0 or current git") and reads inconsistently with the solution typing; the reviewer's option (b) -- rewording it toward c13's "we believe this is fixed, closing" -- would be a fair polish. That is an authoring blemish in one non-graded string, not a measurement-class violation or an unfair-scoring defect.

refuted_claims.claim: The crash-dump clarification is placed downstream of N2_x (the curl 8.5.0 retest), but in the thread that evidence arrived three months before the 8.5.0 retest and came from a reporter still on an 8.0.1-based build, so the graph's clarification chain does not follow the thread's actual order.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The chronology the reviewer cites is accurate -- c18 (participant5) is 2023-09-01 on an 8.0.1-based beta, and the 8.5.0 retest that defines N2_x is c28 (reporter) 2023-12-19 -- but chronology is not the contract's ordering constraint. The contract states explicitly that "a task graph encodes a case's ANSWER KEY, not a transcript," and that ordering is governed by system_state_id (constant while the world is unchanged) plus monotone info_state growth. Every node here is S1: no system change occurs anywhere before the terminal, so no state-machine ordering is violated by placing the dump evidence after the version retests. Containment holds and is machine-validated. The evidence is also version-agnostic in substance: c18's finding (discarded Curl_easy *data_s, invalid data_s->p.http, error_code = NGHTTP2_STREAM_CLOSED in 317/318 reports) is reproduced faithfully in the clarification's user_answer and describes the same crash the reporter still hits on 8.5.0 (c28), so nothing about the 8.0.1 build makes it stale or misleading. The multi-user fold the reviewer implicitly worries about is already declared as the contract requires, in e3's comment: "Evidence from the original reporter and other affected libcurl users is folded into one simulated user side." The proposed fix (adding a provenance note) is at most an optional annotation; there is no defect to correct.

gh_curl_curl_11203.summary: The case tests diagnosing minute-long stalls in curl's Hyper backend down to "a hyper_clientconn is created per request, so an HTTP/2 connection preface is re-sent on a reused connection, provoking GOAWAY", with the practical fix being PR #12191 (disable HTTP/2 for Hyper, fall back to HTTP/1.1). The graph gets the root cause, the fix, and the one genuine dead end (PR #11344) right. Its central flaw is ordering: the reporter's post-fix verification (thread c44/c46, Nov–Dec 2023) is modeled as a clarification edge e4 that sits *before* the solution edge e5, and that post-fix measurement is then hard-required in e5.required_info — so the graph both leaks the answer and penalizes an agent that proposes the correct fix on exactly the evidence participant7 used in the thread. A secondary problem is that a bundled user answer ("the trace does not show a new connection") directly contradicts the graph's own root cause.
gh_curl_curl_11203.strengths: The one blind path in the graph is correctly identified and correctly labelled: PR #11344 was proposed as a fix (c7 "I made some small changes that resolve the slowness for me. Pr in #11344") and genuinely falsified for the reporter (c8 "Does not fix it for @reporter apparently"; c11 "Elapsed: 0:01:01,321" plus "the response of first URL got dropped in some cases"), and the N2_x aftermath node reproduces both the ~61s runtime and the missing-response symptom accurately. The root cause in e5 and satisfaction condition 1 matches the thread's accepted analysis almost word for word (c23's Wireshark preface-per-request comparison and c35's two-problem summary: per-request hyper_clientconn plus silent retry on GOAWAY), and the fix (PR #12191, HTTP/1.1 fallback) plus the "connection-filter rearchitecture needed before restoring H2" caveat matches c41/c42/c40/c45. Measurement-class handling is right: the --trace-ascii capture, the Wireshark capture, the --http1.1 comparison and the rebuild-and-retime are all modeled as clarification edges, not solutions, even though --http1.1 doubles as the eventual workaround. The Task body is a clean opening report with no later knowledge, the L3 clarification answers stay at the level of raw timings/frames with the lifecycle inference correctly parked in info_inferred_by_engineer and inference_hint, the multi-contributor merge is declared on both e1 and e3, and the persona hint matches the reporter's own c3 ("I'm clueless about such internal details").

confirmed_findings.claim: The canonical path forces a clarification (e4, info_id=master_with_hyper_http2_disabled_finishes_near_one_second) that reveals the outcome of the fix before the fix has been proposed: both the question patterns and the user answer presuppose that HTTP/2 has already been disabled in the Hyper backend, which is the very solution the agent is supposed to produce on edge e5.

Thread chronology is fix-then-verify: c41 (participant7, 2023-10-24) 'I think for the short term, we should disable HTTP/2 support in the Hyper integration'; c42 same day 'I've posted #12191 with the quick / temporary fix of disabling HTTP2 with Hyper'; the reporter's rebuild-and-retime report is c44 (2023-11-24) and c46 (2023-12-02). The graph inverts this: e4 (clarification_only, N2->N3) sits BEFORE e5 (the disable-HTTP/2 solution). The leak is not merely inferable, it is textual: question_patterns[0] is 'Can you rebuild current curl and Hyper master after the Hyper HTTP/2 change and rerun the benchmark?', and the info_id itself is literally 'master_with_hyper_http2_disabled_finishes_near_one_second'. The graph's own e4 comment concedes the ordering: 'This is user-run verification of the current master after PR #12191 disabled HTTP/2 for the Hyper backend.' The MEASUREMENT-CLASS rule does defend the edge_type (clarification_only is right for a user-run rebuild-and-time), so the edge type is not the defect — the placement and the fix-naming wording are. An agent standing at N2 is handed the answer key before it is asked for it.

confirmed_findings.claim: The solution's hard required_info includes the post-fix verification result, so an agent that correctly proposes disabling HTTP/2 for the Hyper backend on the pre-fix evidence available at N2 is scored as missing required information.
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: Confirmed on the merits, though it is the downstream half of finding 1 rather than an independent defect. e5.solution.required_info.L3 = [trace_shows_two_approximately_30_second_idle_periods, packet_capture_shows_repeated_h2_preface_per_request, forcing_http11_completes_in_about_300ms, master_with_hyper_http2_disabled_finishes_near_one_second]. The thread shows the accepted fix was reached from the first three alone: c23 (participant4) supplies both the repeated-preface capture ('Curl with hyper sends over: A HTTP2 connection preface ... Request 1, A HTTP2 connection preface ... Request 2 ...') and the '# this takes 300 ms curl --http1.1 ...' comparison; c35 (participant7) adds the GOAWAY analysis; c41 then proposes disabling HTTP/2. Nothing with HTTP/2 disabled had been built or timed at that moment. Note this is NOT a gettability violation — the info_id is a clarification info_id on e4, so the machine check passes; the defect is circularity (the fix's own verification is a precondition for proposing the fix). Downgraded from high because it is entirely resolved by fixing finding 1, and because satisfaction condition 5 already carves out user verification as a separate requirement.

confirmed_findings.claim: N3 keeps system_state_id 'S1' even though it describes the world after the user rebuilt with the fixed master, and its symptoms are already the terminal symptoms; the state id only flips to S2 on e5.

confirmed_findings.claim: e3's question_patterns[1] already names the '30-second waits', a figure not in N2_x's info_state and precisely what this clarification is supposed to surface.

refuted_claims.claim: The bundled user answer on e3 asserts flatly that 'The trace does not show a new connection during those pauses', which contradicts the graph's accepted root cause and satisfaction condition 1 and would steer a reasoning agent away from the correct diagnosis.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The quoted evidence does not support the claim. (a) The sentence is verbatim-faithful to the thread: c17 (participant1, 2023-08-31) 'No, the trace shows no new connection.' It is a real user-side observation, not an invention, and it directly answers the graph's own question_pattern about whether a new connection is opened. (b) There is no contradiction with c23/c35 once the timing is read carefully. c23: the server 'will, either immediately or after a delay of 30 seconds, send a GOAWAY after which curl+hyper sets up a new connection and tries again'. The reconnect therefore happens AFTER the GOAWAY, i.e. at the END of the ~30s idle period — the graph's wording is scoped 'during those pauses', which is exactly the interval in which nothing happens (c12: 'Curl_hyper_stream is called once per second for 30 seconds with select_res of 0' — no IO at all). (c) The reviewer misquotes the answer key: satisfaction condition 1 reads '...provoking server GOAWAY/error handling that caused long delays or dropped requests' and never requires that curl opened a new connection; the 'after which curl+hyper opens a new connection and retries' clause is the reviewer's own embellishment. Also note the two observations are at different instrument levels (curl ascii trace vs. decrypted Wireshark capture), so an agent is not being fed a denial of anything the answer key demands.

refuted_claims.claim: The terminal presents the case as resolved without reflecting that the underlying defect stayed open: HTTP/2 with Hyper remained broken and the issue was closed as KNOWN_BUGS material.

The graph is a faithful and unusually well-constructed rendering of that arc: the browser/channel narrowing, master-channel test, about:gpu + raw shader dump, JPEG-vs-PNG/WebP/GIF isolation, the BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false probe, and the corrected-Chrome verification all map to real thread turns in the right order, and the root cause and satisfaction conditions match what participant3 and participant23 established. No blind path is mislabeled in a way that inverts the answer, and every required_info id is obtainable. The remaining issues are fidelity-level: the one blind path presents a one-sided outcome for a workaround that the thread says worked for most reporters, it dead-ends, and a couple of state/merge bookkeeping details are loose.
gh_flutter_flutter_140504.strengths: Root cause and satisfaction conditions are exactly what the thread established: participant2's early guess (c17, Metal shader compiler regression on macOS 14), participant3's c60 "The bug is somewhere between ANGLE and Metal deep inside Chromium", c72 (ANGLE-Metal experiment disabled on Intel Macs) and c75/c79 (Chrome 122.0.6261.129 / chromium issue 328302269). gh_moby_moby_49498.summary: The case tests a Docker 28.0.0 firewall-rule-ordering regression surfacing as containers losing Tailscale connectivity, where the real culprit is Tailscale's stateful-filtering DROP in ts-forward being reached before Docker's per-bridge ACCEPT. The fidelity breaks at the end: the graph makes "upgrade to Docker 28.0.1" the mandated durable fix for the Tailscale scenario and demotes disabling stateful filtering to a temporary workaround, whereas in the thread the maintainer doubted a rule rearrangement would fix the Tailscale case, no Tailscale participant ever tested 28.0.1, and the reporter's confirmed resolution was `--stateful-filtering=false`. The 28.0.1 verification is also placed as a prerequisite clarification before the edge that proposes 28.0.1, inverting the thread's order.
gh_moby_moby_49498.strengths: The #1 historical defect is absent and, better, correctly handled: e2 (`iptables -I DOCKER-USER -j ts-forward` / `iptables -D FORWARD -j ts-forward`) is marked is_known_blind_path=true and it is a genuine falsified attempt — proposed in c6 by the maintainer and reported failed in c7 by participant2 ("didnt help for me"); the aftermath node N1_x and the "must not present this as the complete fix" satisfaction condition match the thread exactly. The measurement-class rule is applied well: both the stateful-filtering setting check (c33 -> c34/c36) and the `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false` toggle probe (c36/c39) are clarification_only edges with the toggle's result as the user_answer, with an explicit comment explaining why the toggle-that-doubles-as-workaround stays a clarification. The multi-user merge (reporter + participant2 + the non-Tailscale 28.0.1 verifiers) is declared in the e1 and e5 comments and in persona_hint. The Task body is clean — it carries only the reporter's opening DNS/resolv.conf framing and the 27.5.1 rollback, with no leak of stateful filtering, iptables ordering, or 28.0.1. The clarification chain order (direct-IP test -> bridge config -> iptables dump -> blind rule move -> stateful-filtering check -> toggle probe) reproduces the thread's real diagnostic sequence, the e1 answers are faithful to c1/c3/c5/c13, and the safety warning against deleting Docker's DROP rules or flushing chains is lifted correctly from c6 ("deleting the rule means allowing anything to reach the container from outside the host"). persona_hint matches the reporter's c3 self-correction away from the DNS theory. refuted_claims.claim: The graph mandates "Docker 28.0.1 or later" as the durable fix for the Tailscale + stateful-filtering case and demotes `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false` to a mere temporary workaround, but the thread never establishes that 28.0.1 fixes the Tailscale scenario — the maintainer explicitly doubted it, and the only resolution actually confirmed for this reporter was disabling stateful filtering.

Nothing about the causal story is misattributed. The objection is only about which remedy is scored as durable. There the thread supports the graph: c33's doubt is scoped to "a simple rearrangement of the moby 28.0 rules", and it is superseded by the same maintainer at c50 — "I believe all the issues here will be addressed by some combination of [49518] and [49538]" — followed by closing the issue as completed (the tailscale case was item 1 of his own c21 issue list). c31 already describes the actual 28.0.1 design (split Docker's rules out of FORWARD into a new chain jumped at the top), which is what restores the per-bridge ACCEPT ahead of the ts-forward jump seen failing in c13/c36 — so 28.0.1 is technically expected to cover this scenario, and c51 (an affected reporter) says the tailscale issue "was the same as was also affecting us after all". TS-2024-005 - I'll continue to investigate"). Per authoring rule 4c release facts are legitimate content of concrete_example. So c49/c50-before-c51 is not a constraint the graph must reproduce. (b) Edge typing: rule 4 (MEASUREMENT-CLASS) lists "version checks" and "test/try builds" as clarification_only "even when the probed toggle doubles as a workaround" — an upgrade-and-verify probe is the textbook case, and the graph applies the identical treatment to the stateful-filtering toggle at e4 with an explicit comment. (c) required_info: the id is a clarification info_id on e5, so it is gettable under the stated gettability rule, and rule 1 grades "must be asked for or measured" facts as L3, which is what e6 does. The resulting answer key — you must have an affected host actually confirm 28.0.1 before you declare the durable fix — is also what satisfaction_conditions[5] demands and what rule 7 requires (user verification before declaring resolution).

Rule 9 requires all affected users to be folded into ONE simulated user with the merge noted in the edge comment, and e5's comment does exactly that, naming the sources ("internal-routing and pre-existing firewall-rule-order failures") and stating that the original reporter's verification was the stateful-filtering interaction on Docker 28. refuted_claims.claim: N3 sets user_perceives_resolved=false even though N3 is exactly the state where the reporter declared the problem solved.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The proposed fix is not what the field means in this codebase. user_simulator/responder.py:_apply_satisfaction sets termination_reason='premature_satisfaction' whenever a non-terminal destination node has user_perceives_resolved=true, and simulator.py:_TERMINAL_REASONS includes 'premature_satisfaction', so is_terminal() returns True — the session ENDS on arrival.
